items.prompt:
Healthy ecosystems tend to be
A) relatively stable over time
B) always collapsing
C) empty
D) frozen

What keeps an ecosystem relatively stable?
A) Complex interactions among organisms
B) Having no organisms
C) Constant fires
D) Removing all predators

A big enough change in conditions can
A) turn an ecosystem into a new one
B) never change anything
C) create energy
D) stop time
items.answer: A) turn an ecosystem into a new one

steps: Large changes can create a new ecosystem.

items.prompt:
Which is a disturbance that could change an ecosystem?
A) A major fire
B) A gentle breeze
C) One sunny day
D) A single leaf falling

Predators help keep an ecosystem stable by
A) keeping prey populations in check
B) eating all plants
C) removing water
D) adding pollution
items.answer: A) keeping prey populations in check

items.prompt:
Steady fish and plant populations in a pond for ten years are evidence of
A) a stable ecosystem
B) a dying ecosystem
C) no ecosystem
D) pollution

Evaluate: 'Any small change destroys an ecosystem.' This claim is
A) too strong, because ecosystems absorb small changes and only large changes tend to create a new ecosystem
B) always true
C) proof ecosystems never change
D) about weather only
items.answer: A) too strong, because ecosystems absorb small changes and only large changes tend to create a new ecosystem

items.prompt:
A disease wipes out a key species and the ecosystem changes. This shows that
A) a large change can shift a stable ecosystem into a new one
B) ecosystems never change
C) key species do not matter
D) small changes always destroy ecosystems
items.answer: A) a large change can shift a stable ecosystem into a new one

steps: Losing a key species is a large change.
